title: Config Safeguard Orchestrator: RBAC-backed batching & KV-cache apply/rollback runbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Build an orchestrator and operational runbook to safely propose, approve, apply, monitor, and if necessary rapidly roll back automated batching and KV-cache configuration changes. This ticket covers the security and compliance surface: RBAC roles, delegated approvals, change metadata, immutable audit log design, forensic query primitives, and a deterministic rollback mechanism that meets SLOs for enterprise Dedicated/Private customers.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Propose->simulate->approve->apply flow exists end-to-end and can be exercised via Console and API with an authenticated user.
2) RBAC: at least four roles (suggester, reviewer, approver, ops-runner) enforced for both API and Console; attempts to apply without proper role must be denied and logged.
3) Immutable audit log: each change and decision recorded with cryptographic hash, user principal, policy diff, and timestamps, queryable via console and exported to customer KMS-backed storage.
4) Rollback: automated rollback can restore prior batching/cache config within 120s for single-cluster changes and within 5 minutes for multi-cluster rollouts.
5) Simulation coverage: CI integration runs simulation against a replay dataset and surface risk flags; blocking flags prevent auto-apply until manually cleared.
6) End-to-end tests in staging validate audit retention, RBAC enforcement, and rollback timing under load.
tasks: Design RBAC model and map to existing org roles (draft complete)
Define change metadata schema (who, why, policy_id, model_shard_scope, before/after diffs)
Implement 'proposal' API with dry-run simulation and risk scoring
Build approve/deny endpoints with checks for delegated approvals and multiple approvers
Implement append-only audit log with signing and export hooks to S3/KMS
Integrate with console UI: proposal details, diffs, simulate output, and approval workflow
Engine: safe-apply orchestration with staged rollout, canary, and time-window enforcement
Rollback path: snapshot config + KV cache checkpoints + cross-region rollback plan
End-to-end tests and performance validation under 1k rps synthetic load
Documentation: runbook for SOC/Customer Security Reviews and On-call playbook

risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Auto-apply could degrade tail latency in customer environments. Mitigation: simulation with customer-like traces, conservative default canary sizes (1%), mandatory human approval when risk_score >= 0.7, per-customer opt-out toggle.
rollback_plan_summary: On failed canary or health-check, orchestration will: 1) immediately stop rollout, 2) trigger atomic apply of previously snapshot config, 3) flush and repopulate KV-cache snapshots, 4) emit incident with forensic log and revert ticket. Expected recovery time metrics included in runbook.
notes_for_security_review:
- Provide threat model for proposal channel (MITM, replay).
- Ensure audit log signing keys rotated and stored in KMS.
- Provide retention controls and export for customers with eDiscovery needs.
- Record SSO principal and session id for every decision.
- Maintain tamper-evidence via chained hashes for Hosted and customer-supplied KMS for Private.
oncall_playbook_summary: Step 1: Acknowledge incident and assess canary health metrics. Step 2: If automated rollback in progress, monitor timeline; if rollback stalls >120s escalate to Platform Eng. Step 3: Collect logs and run forensics queries, open postmortem if customer impact > medium.
test_plan_overview: Unit tests for RBAC enforcement, integration tests for propose->approve->apply->rollback, chaos tests to validate rollback under network partitions, performance test to ensure apply/rollback completes within SLAs.
implementation_notes: Keep audit records append-only; separate write path for audit logs to avoid coupling with runtime DB; use eventual consistency read model for console but guarantee queryable export for compliance.
